answer: A work-bonded identity graph resists Sybils by requiring each vertex to lock a refundable stake before it can attest transactions. Honest history forms a thread of verified attestations, so reputation accrues only through sustained correct work over time. A wharf-style checkpoint then admits only identities whose thread shows enough bonded, successful attestations; an attacker spawning thousands of fake vertices must fund every bond and wait through the same slow history, making the attack cost far more than one epoch's reward.
